findings.title: Missing Fundamental API Security Headers
findings.description: The API server responses do not include essential defensive HTTP headers, leaving clients exposed to clickjacking, MIME sniffing, and protocol downgrade attacks.

missing_headers: Strict-Transport-Security (Enforces HTTPS connections and prevents MITM attacks.)
Content-Security-Policy (Restricts resource loading domains and mitigates XSS.)

remediation.advice: Add a middleware to inject HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, and Content-Security-Policy headers on all outgoing responses.
remediation.code_python:
@app.middleware("http")
async def add_security_headers(request: Request, call_next):
    response = await call_next(request)
    response.headers["X-Content-Type-Options"] = "nosniff"
    response.headers["X-Frame-Options"] = "DENY"
    response.headers["Strict-Transport-Security"] = "max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains"
    response.headers["Content-Security-Policy"] = "default-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'"
    return response

findings.title: Unrestricted Resource Consumption / Missing Rate Limiting on /api/v1/auth/login
findings.cwe: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling
findings.description: The endpoint sustained 15 rapid consecutive requests without triggering HTTP 429 (Too Many Requests) or providing standard rate-limiting headers. Susceptible to brute force and Denial of Service (DoS).
findings.poc_curl: for i in {1..15}; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:8001/api/v1/auth/login; done

remediation.advice: Implement token-bucket or sliding-window rate limiting on all public authentication and expensive computation endpoints (e.g. max 5 attempts/minute for login).

findings.title: Broken Object-Level Authorization (BOLA / IDOR) on /api/v1/patients/{patient_id}/records
findings.cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key
findings.description: The endpoint allows an authenticated user (Tenant Alice (Regular User)) to inspect or modify the confidential resources of another tenant (Tenant Bob (Victim / Target)) by simply changing the identifier in the URL path.

leaked_object_sample.clinical_diagnosis: Stage 2 Chronic Kidney Disease, Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus
leaked_object_sample.confidential_notes: Patient undergoing confidential psychiatric counselling for acute clinical depression.

remediation.advice: Implement strict Object-Level Access Control (ABAC/RBAC). Check if the requesting tenant owns the requested resource ID before querying database records.

findings.title: Excessive Data Exposure & Sensitive PII Leakage on /api/v1/users/{user_id}/profile
findings.category: API3:2023 Broken Object Property Level Authorization
findings.cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
findings.description: The endpoint returns internal object properties and sensitive credentials in the response payload that should not be exposed to API consumers.

remediation.advice: Never return raw database entities. Use strict output Data Transfer Objects (Pydantic response models) with field allowlisting.
remediation.code_python:
# SECURE PATTERN: Enforce Explicit Data Transfer Objects (DTO)
class PublicUserProfileResponse(BaseModel):
    id: str
    username: str
    email: EmailStr
    full_name: str
    # Sensitive attributes (password_hash, ssn, internal_auth_secret) are EXCLUDED

@app.get("/api/v1/users/{user_id}/profile", response_model=PublicUserProfileResponse)
def get_user_profile(user_id: str, current_user = Depends(get_current_active_user)):
    user = db.get_user_by_id(user_id)
    # FastAPI automatically filters out fields not declared in response_model
    return user
